name: stat-tile
purpose: A KPI tile: a label, one big figure that counts up into place with an optional muted unit, an optional delta `Tag` against a named period, and an optional sparkline that bleeds to the tile's edges along its bottom. The delta reads good or bad for the metric, not merely up or down: `inverse` flips the polarity for metrics where a rise is bad (threats, errors, latency). A row of tiles sits above a dashboard's charts; without a `trend` the tile is the figure alone, the shape a usage strip uses. Inside a `StatTileGroup` the tiles become the cells of one card, split by dividers, with the delta aligned to the cell's end. `kind` picks the figure face: `mono` (the big-number mono figure of a usage strip) or `sans` (the large heading figure of a traffic summary).
useWhen: The headline numbers of a dashboard: total requests, blocked threats, cache hit ratio, error rate.
A single value whose change matters more than its history; the sparkline adds the shape of that history.
avoidWhen: The history itself is the point → use `chart`.
A share of a whole → use `donut-chart`.
Marketing figures on a site band → use `big-numbers`.
related: chart` — the full history behind a tile.
chart-card` — the box for a chart; a tile is its own small surface and does not sit in one.
big-numbers` — the marketing figure band, with no delta and no live data.
spark-chart` — the sparkline the tile draws its `trend` with; use it alone for a trend beside a number in a list or table.
tag` — the delta renders as a `Tag`; the empty band's "No data" is a `Tag` too.
divider` — carries the "No data" `Tag` across the empty band.
stat-tile-group` — one card split into cells, one per tile: the KPI strip of an overview.
bestPractices: Name the comparison period in `deltaLabel` ("vs previous 24 hours"); a bare percentage is ambiguous.
Set `inverse` on every metric where a rise is bad, so a growing threat count reads as a regression.
Keep the label in sentence case with no trailing colon.
Put the unit in `unit` ("GB", "ms", "%"), not inside `formatValue`, so it reads muted beside the figure.
Leave `trend` out for a strip of figures with no history; the tile then has no chart band.
Give the sparkline the same buckets as the chart below it, about twelve points.

For a KPI strip that reads as one band (an overview's usage row), put the tiles in a `StatTileGroup`; do not hand-build the card, the grid or the dividers. Separate tiles are for figures that stand alone.
Use `kind="mono"` (default) for usage figures with a delta, `kind="sans"` for a summary row of plain figures (requests, data transferred, error rate) above its charts. Keep one kind per row.
Pass the delta as the raw percentage (`12.4`); the tile prints at most two decimals and drops trailing zeros (`+12.4%`, `+3%`).

props.name: label
props.doc: Metric name, in sentence case. Fallback for the default slot.

props.name: value
props.doc: The current value. It counts up from the previous value on change; null renders a dash.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Figure face: `mono` is the big-number mono figure, `sans` the large heading figure.

props.name: unit
props.doc: Unit read after the figure, smaller and in a muted sans tone. Empty hides it.

props.name: delta
props.doc: Signed change against the named period, in percent, printed with at most two decimals and no trailing zeros. Null hides the delta.

props.name: deltaLabel
props.doc: The comparison period, read after the delta.

props.name: inverse
props.doc: A rise is bad for this metric; flips the delta between success and danger.

props.name: trend
props.doc: Sparkline values, oldest first. Empty hides the sparkline.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders Skeleton lines in place of the figure, delta and sparkline.

slots.name: aside
slots.notes: Trailing content beside the label, such as an info icon or a menu.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import StatTile from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile'
</script>

<template>
  <StatTile
    label="Blocked threats"
    :value="48210"
    :delta="12.4"
    delta-label="vs previous 24 hours"
    inverse
    :trend="[310, 290, 340, 380, 360, 420, 410, 470, 450, 520, 500, 560]"
  />
</template>
